title: Illustration / Characters / Arms and hands / Please don’t…
slide_intent: Reject unnecessary hand complexity and broken limb construction so a gesture remains coherent and easy to maintain.
strategic_value: Specific negative examples can help Duolingo keep character hands consistent across different illustrators.
demonstration: Five crossed panels show rejected arm or finger constructions, beside a five-item prohibition list.
practical_value: Audit the arm-to-hand connection, forearm length and finger count before finalizing a gesture.

content_islands.name: Rejected constructions
content_islands.spec: Arrange three crossed arm examples above two crossed isolated hands at left, matching the subjects in the warning list.

content_islands.name: Prohibition list
content_islands.spec: Place the Please Don’t heading and five warnings at right, including the maximum finger count.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text explains that unnecessary fingers add more detail to keep track of.
reference_purposes.Application: Five rejected examples demonstrate the listed construction problems.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source prohibits excess or unnecessary fingers, shortened forearms, detached hands and more than four fingers.

ingredient.name: Arm and hand construction limits
ingredient.role: Preserve coherent limbs with no unnecessary detail.
ingredient.application: Keep the hand connected to the arm, avoid shortening the forearm, and use only necessary fingers with a maximum of four.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. Applies to the displayed character illustration system; the limit should not be generalized to all brands or anatomical drawing.
